timing measurement or timing comparison. D-150 remains provisionally closed by D-153.

`controlContext`'s definition is only a lookup. No remaining production call
passes its result to local probe, verification, Apply, persistence or cleanup.
Boot records its caller-bound context separately under `bootCallerKey`; the
independent local budget remains available for safe cleanup after TERM.
Repeated hung requests preserve local safety and serving before D, and the
manual-clock unit proof stops at exactly D. Signed/kernel deadlines are not
extended. A real local check failure still fails closed.

## Closed recovery schedule and containment

A closed recovery flushes the existing truthful ready/provisional observation.
The next grant request remains at its existing D-067 slot. For the reviewed
5-second heartbeat scenario, that is 5 seconds after the previous request send,
minus time already spent recovering. General local waiting is at most 60 seconds
from that send, reduced by the lease renewal lead. Retry-After is an independent
lower bound and can exceed 60 seconds. Ongoing bounded work, request latency and
central eligibility are not a guarantee of serving within that local wait.

There is no immediate extra request or schedule reset. For newly issued leases,
the minimum normal grant-less interval is `min(heartbeat, 60s, time to renewal
lead)`; with supported heartbeat values and a fresh minimum 60-second lease it
is at least 1 second, and is 5 seconds in the reviewed fixture. Subsequent waits
double to the existing 60-second cap. Replayed leases past their lead and failed
requests retain the existing cadence/Retry-After rules. Existing generation,
identity-freeze and first-lease exceptions are unchanged; this is not a new
global rate limiter. There is at most the existing one renewal attempt per Step
outside those previously defined exceptions.

`runStepDelay` no longer combines the due grant-less slot with an earlier
start-anchored poll tick. Longer waits still allow ordinary closed-state polls.
Those polls freshly verify the unchanged empty recovery model under the node
lock, and do not reinstall a baseline. Both bindings and leases are empty, no
probe exception exists, and signed inputs and other safety gates still qualify.
Every other model input is compared. Only clock samples are normalized because
this empty model has no admission timeout. Drift, changed configuration or a
new failure takes the ordinary fail-closed path. A populated lease still needs
a fresh full Apply and verification before serving. D-067 revision 11 and D-126
reporting are unchanged.

A quarantine attempt and its verified baseline are scoped to the Step's local
budget. Apply's own quarantine counts. A failed containment baseline can still
be repaired by withdrawal; successful repair is reused for the rest of that
pass. Apply and probe-rule mutation invalidate baseline reuse. The following
Step gets a fresh budget and containment audit. No enforce production file was
changed, and D-090/D-106 held proofs continue to pass.

## R23 boot heartbeat

The reported `agent: boot failed: heartbeat: context deadline exceeded` names
`bootHeartbeat`'s 100 ms child deadline. Follow-up 47's retained excerpt reports
the entire failing subcase at 0.54 seconds, excluding exhaustion of Boot's
10-second parent budget. `WriteHeartbeatContext` creates a file,
writes, chmods, fsyncs and closes it before checking the context immediately
before rename. Disk latency or scheduler delay can exhaust that child even
while Boot's 10-second allowance remains live. The old log does not identify
which of Boot's three heartbeat calls or which syscall was delayed; those
finer details are not asserted.

The fix removes the second deadline rather than increasing a timeout or
retrying. Boot still has one 10-second local budget; Close retains its separate
3-second allowance. No expired heartbeat may be atomically published. A writer
seam lets the new test assert exact equality with the parent deadline and then
prove canceled publication leaves the prior receipt untouched. It uses no
sleep. The original eight interrupted-checkpoint cases are unchanged.

## D-150 code reading only

**Not determined.** No frozen arm was run. The frozen `567080be` code already
calls `kernel.rejectedGeneration` before generation repair/withdrawal
(`node/agent/serving.go:71` and `:133`), and the counter-discontinuity mechanism
in `meterreset.go` remains present in `28e9e41c`. Follow-ups 37–43 did replace
the `finalDone` gate at `567080be:node/agent/engine.go:1060` with independent
`epochClosed` preparation at `28e9e41c:node/agent/engine.go:1266`, and added
settlement tracking in `usage.go:322`. That change addresses interrupted closed
epoch recovery, but the supplied snapshot already has an open
`after_final_sample` epoch and generation 3 with no discontinuity. It does not
identify that interruption or establish why the discontinuity is missing.

No specific replaced change can be attributed from this code reading and the
supplied final snapshot. The failed frozen scenario remains failed. Nothing is
claimed about 37–43's timing or about the difference between the two supplied
run durations.

## Functional lab and validation

The single ordinary lab **failed: 12 passed, 1 failed, 1 optional skip**.
`TestLabD087_D104_GrantRenewalExpiryCorrelation` reached the existing assertion
at `tests/netlab/agent/timing-analysis.py:117`: the last-positive lower bound was
false, while the first-drop upper bound was true. No rerun was made. No cause or
attribution to these changes is assigned. Automatic scenario captures are
retained in `.agent/f48/lab-capture`; their hashes and the failed output are in
the validation record. This is a failed functional gate, not a timing comparison.
The optional D116 installer-marker scenario skipped with its opt-in unset.
Owned Docker inventory after cleanup is empty in all four object classes.
The pre-lab suite check found no concurrent assembled run: zero wait (the check
itself took 0.015 seconds).

Admission audit limitation: all top-level commands and PATH-resolved Go/Docker
commands used isolated admission checks, but GNU Make selected `/usr/bin/make`
for internal recursive Make launches in the lab. Those launches inherited the
admitted run rather than receiving separate wrapper checks. This is recorded as
a process-compliance gap, not claimed as complete per-command admission. The
remaining driver explicitly pins `MAKE` to the admission wrapper. No reservation
was acquired, and the failed scenario was not rerun to change this record.


Results are recorded after the gates in
`followup48-validation-2026-11-03.json`. The ordinary lab uses only
`FVPN_LAB_PREFIX=fvpn-w2-agent-core-f48`; no measurement reservation or paired
run is involved. All owned containers, images, networks and volumes are checked
for removal afterward.

No ordinary scenario stops the whole central control plane with desired-state
requests hanging. The lab does have held lease-renewal requests: fakecontrol's
lease handler waits for `/release` or request cancellation (`handlers.go:350`),
used by restart/kernel-expiry cases. That is narrower than F20-01's hung
desired-state request consuming the budget before the local probe. The r28 and
new repeated-hang unit proofs are the evidence for that boundary.
